overview:
Maryland's 2nd District leans Democratic by about ten points, and incumbent Johnny Olszewski is seeking re-election with a decisive financial edge. He has raised roughly $1.24 million and holds about $644,000 on hand, while Republican Dave Wallace has raised under $30,000 with about $7,000 available. No outside groups have spent against the incumbent, and prediction markets put his re-election odds near 95 percent.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and market pricing. Those indicators all point the same direction: a comfortable Democratic margin in the low twenties. Neither party has shown signs of investing to make this race competitive, and the challenger's minimal fundraising leaves little obvious path to close the gap before Election Day.
